name: Scale out
summary: Weighted load balancer, three app servers, one shared Valkey, MongoDB Atlas.

name: Edge protection
summary: CDN and WAF at the edge, an API gateway, and rate limits split across layers.
changes: Edge network with CDN and WAF in front of everything
API gateway with API keys and a coarse per-IP limit
"Which layer limits what" table, and the client IP through the proxy chain
Failure rows for the edge, gateway and load balancer services

name: Database fault tolerance
summary: MongoDB replica set across three zones, oplog replication and automatic failover.
changes: How a write reaches the other copies: primary, oplog, majority acknowledgement
Failover timeline: election in about 12 s, driver retries the write once
Driver settings: mongodb+srv, retryWrites, w: majority, read preference
Failure rows for losing the MongoDB primary or a secondary

name: Blog service, one login
summary: Cognito sign-in shared by every service, and a GraphQL blog on AppSync and Lambda using its own database in the same cluster.
changes: Amazon Cognito user pool: one sign-in, one token for REST and GraphQL
Blog service on AWS AppSync with Lambda resolvers
Separate blog database and DB user in the same Atlas cluster
GraphQL schema, resolver map and design decisions
Failure rows for Cognito, AppSync and the shared connection limit

name: Team stacks, blog media
summary: Each team owns its own stack: the blog gets its own Valkey, and blog images go to S3 behind CloudFront.
changes: Ownership split: REST team and blog team stacks, shared login, edge and cluster
Valkey "blog" for post cache, per-user limits and view counters
S3 blog-media with direct uploads through signed URLs, and an image processor
What's cached, how big it gets, and the eviction policy
Failure rows for each Valkey, the image processor and media delivery
